label: Democritus reconciled changeless Being with change via moving atoms in void
description: Democritus and Leucippus resolved the Eleatic dilemma of changeless Being by positing infinite, indivisible, unchangeable particles (atoms) moving continuously through that which is not (the void).
dialecticalTension: How change and multiplicity can exist if Being cannot come from Non-Being: resolved by asserting Void as physical space.
historicalContext: 5th century BCE Abdera and Elea. Democritus synthesized Eleatic ontology with Ionian natural philosophy.

citations.author: Democritus
citations.quote: By convention sweet, by convention bitter, by convention color: but in reality atoms and void.

label: Defended Parmenidean monism through dialectical reductio paradoxes
description: Zeno of Elea adopted Parmenides of Elea's insights and systematically extended them into new metaphysical, ethical, or epistemological domains.
dialecticalTension: Negotiating the intellectual shift from Parmenides of Elea's perspective to Zeno of Elea's reconstructed system.
historicalContext: Direct contemporaneous dialogue and pedagogical transmission during the Pre-Socratic era.
